definitions.explanation: The act of translating Japanese text into English. Commonly encountered as a section in English language textbooks and exams in Japan.

examples.japanese: {和文英訳|わぶんえいやく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{和文英訳|わぶんえいやく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: A Japanese-to-English translation question appeared at the end of the exam.

examples.japanese: {和文英訳|わぶんえいやく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{直訳|ちょくやく}→直訳：13629_chokuyaku⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：09578_dehanaku⟧、⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧な⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: In Japanese-to-English translation, what matters is writing natural English, not translating word for word.

notes:
A four-character compound: ⟦{和文|わぶん}→和文：16805_wabun⟧ (Japanese text) + ⟦{英訳|えいやく}→英訳：16317_eiyaku⟧ (English translation). Frequently encountered in English education in Japan, where {和文英訳|わぶんえいやく} exercises are a standard part of the curriculum from junior high school through university entrance exams.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和文英訳|わぶんえいやく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧: J-to-E translation question
- {和文英訳|わぶんえいやく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧: J-to-E translation practice
- {和文英訳|わぶんえいやく}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to translate from Japanese to English

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {英文和訳|えいぶんわやく}: English-to-Japanese translation — the reverse direction
- ⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧: translation — general term for any translation
- ⟦{通訳|つうやく}→通訳：03516_tsuuyaku⟧: interpretation — oral translation, not written
- ⟦{直訳|ちょくやく}→直訳：13629_chokuyaku⟧: literal translation — word-for-word rendering
- ⟦{意訳|いやく}→意訳：17846_iyaku⟧: free translation — capturing meaning over form
